edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the variant readings it marks are left out.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，删去其所注异文。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died in 742.

note.en: Twenty characters, two lines of view and two of advice, and Chinese children usually learn it before they can write. The last couplet is the reason: if you want to see further, go up one more floor. Wikisource notes that an early anthology, the Guoxiu ji, gives the poem to a Zhu Bin; most readers still know it as Wang Zhihuan’s.
note.zh: 二十个字，两句写景，两句说理，中国孩子往往还不会写字就会背。原因就在后两句：想看得更远，就再上一层楼。维基文库注明，早期的选本《国秀集》把这首诗归在朱斌名下；大多数读者仍把它当作王之涣的作品。

excerpt.orig: 欲窮千里目，更上一層樓。
excerpt.en: To see a thousand li further, / climb one more storey of the tower.
excerpt.zh: 欲穷千里目，更上一层楼。

gloss.en: Sinks behind the mountains; 盡, used up, gone.
gloss.zh: 依：依傍。尽：消失。太阳傍着山落下去。

gloss.en: Stork Tower stood at Puzhou (present-day Yongji in Shanxi), above the Yellow River; the sea itself is far beyond sight.
gloss.zh: 鹳雀楼故址在蒲州（今山西永济），下临黄河；大海远在视线之外。

gloss.en: 窮: to reach the end of. To see as far as a thousand li.
gloss.zh: 穷：尽，使达到极点。千里目：看到千里之远。

gloss.en: 更: further, once more. Shen Kuo recorded that the tower had three storeys, with the Zhongtiao Mountains in front and the great river below.
gloss.zh: 更：再。沈括《梦溪笔谈》记鹳雀楼“三层，前瞻中条，下瞰大河”。

note.en: Both couplets are strictly parallel, a vast view and then plain advice, and ‘one more floor’ has become a lasting figure for wanting to see further.
note.zh: 两联皆对仗，先写万里之景，再给一句平常的劝勉；“更上一层楼”成了想看得更远的永久说法。
